import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 832

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/832](https://www.erdosproblems.com/832)
- [AkSh16] Akolzin, Ilia and Shabanov, Dmitry, Colorings of hypergraphs with large number of colors.
  Discrete Math. (2016), 3020--3031.
- [Al85] Alon, Noga, Hypergraphs with high chromatic number. Graphs Combin. (1985), 387--389.
- [ChPe20] Cherkashin, Danila and Petrov, Fedor, Regular behavior of the maximal hypergraph
  chromatic number. SIAM J. Discrete Math. (2020), 1326--1333.
-/

namespace Erdos832

open Filter Asymptotics

/--
Let $r\geq 3$ and $k$ be sufficiently large in terms of $r$. Is it true that every $r$-uniform
hypergraph with chromatic number $k$ has at least
$$\binom{(r-1)(k-1)+1}{r}$$
edges, with equality only for the complete graph on $(r-1)(k-1)+1$ vertices?

This was disproved by Alon [Al85]. The validity of this conjecture for $r=3$ remains open.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_832 :
    answer(False) ↔ ∀ r : ℕ, 3 ≤ r → ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop,
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (H : Finset (Finset (Fin n))),
      H.IsUniform r → H.HasHypergraphChromaticNumber k →
      ((r - 1) * (k - 1) + 1).choose r ≤ H.card ∧
      (H.card = ((r - 1) * (k - 1) + 1).choose r →
        ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), S.card = (r - 1) * (k - 1) + 1 ∧ H = S.powersetCard r) := by
  sorry

end Erdos832

reformulations.difference: The equality case uses an arbitrary ambient type Fin n and requires H = S.powersetCard r for a subset S of the prescribed size, rather than requiring the ambient vertex count itself to equal that size.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Erdős–Lovász defines a hypergraph as a collection of sets and its points as the elements of those edges. Thus the relevant vertices are the incident support, not unused ambient labels. Put m = (r - 1) * (k - 1) + 1. For r ≥ 3 and k ≥ 2, one has 1 ≤ r ≤ m. The union of all r-subsets of an m-element S is S. Consequently, the Lean equality condition is equivalent to (H.biUnion id).card = m together with H = (H.biUnion id).powersetCard r, exactly completeness on the source's vertex set. The support equivalence and equivalence of ambient/support colorability for a nonempty palette were proved in the scratch file. Small palette exceptions can be excluded by the eventual threshold. The reverse implication from this complete-edge-family condition to the stated edge-count equality also follows from card_powersetCard.

sources_consulted: P. Erdős, Some old and new problems in various branches of combinatorics (1979), §1, manuscript pp. 3–4: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1979-18.pdf
N. Alon, Hypergraphs with high chromatic number, Graphs and Combinatorics 1 (1985), 387–389: https://web.math.princeton.edu/~nalon/PDFS/Publications/Hypergraphs%20with%20high%20chromatic%20number.pdf

D. Cherkashin and F. Petrov, Regular behaviour of the maximal hypergraph chromatic number, arXiv:1808.01482v4, Introduction and Further questions; LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1808.01482v4 ; abstract/version history: https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.01482
P. Erdős and L. Lovász, Problems and results on 3-chromatic hypergraphs and some related questions (1975), especially the definitions on p. 609: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1975-34.pdf
Rényi Institute's collected Erdős papers index: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html

Akolzin–Shabanov (2016), bibliographic metadata only, obtained through Crossref's title lookup and https://api.openalex.org/works/https://doi.org/10.1016/j.disc.2016.06.016 ; full text was unavailable.
review.notes: No mathematical defects found in the sole declaration. The threshold for k correctly depends on r but not on n or H. Uniformity, weak coloring, exact chromatic number, binomial bounds, equality, answer polarity, and degenerate cases were checked. Alon's disproof supports both answer(False) and research solved; the unresolved special case r = 3 does not contradict the general negative answer. Scratch checks compiled without errors or warnings, including complete 3-graphs, empty cases, and the Fano-plane exception at k = 3. The live erdosproblems.com page returned Cloudflare 403 responses despite descriptive user agents, and AkSh16's full text was unavailable. The original posed claim, including uniqueness, was instead verified in Erdős (1979), with the disproof and subsequent discussion checked in Alon and Cherkashin–Petrov. No declaration remained mathematically unsettled by these access limitations. The reviewed file is unchanged and matches the supplied commit.
